theme: 3 terms on looking at types while the app runs: the real type behind a value, the type of a type, and a tool that lists a value's properties

terms.definition: The real type of a value while the app runs, which can be more specific than the type it was declared with.
terms.example: The array is declared as `[Animal]`, but the Runtime Type of the first item is `Dog`.

terms.definition: The type of a type, written like `Dog.Type`, whose value `Dog.self` lets you pass a type around like any other value.
terms.example: Pass the Metatype into `register`, so the factory knows which type to create.

terms.definition: A Swift type that lets code look at the stored properties of any value, with their names and values, while the app runs.
terms.example: The debug screen uses a Mirror, so new properties show up without extra code.

quizzes.question: Which type lets code list the stored properties of any value while the app runs?

video.title: Runtime Type, Metatype & Mirror | Day 74
video.description:
Learn to explain how Swift looks at types while the app runs: Runtime Type, Metatype & Mirror, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Runtime Type - The real type of a value while the app runs, which can be more specific than the type it was declared with.
Metatype - The type of a type, written like `Dog.Type`, whose value `Dog.self` lets you pass a type around like any other value.
Mirror - A Swift type that lets code look at the stored properties of any value, with their names and values, while the app runs.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Day 74 of the iOS Daily English series: 3 terms a day, from Swift basics to advanced iOS.

landscape.title: Swift Runtime Type, Metatype & Mirror | Day 74
landscape.description:
Explain Runtime Type, Metatype & Mirror in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
런타임 타입, 메타타입, Mirror 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Runtime Type - The real type of a value while the app runs, which can be more specific than the type it was declared with.
한국어: 런타임 타입: 앱이 실행되는 동안 값이 실제로 가진 타입으로, 선언된 타입보다 더 구체적일 수 있음

Metatype - The type of a type, written like `Dog.Type`, whose value `Dog.self` lets you pass a type around like any other value.
한국어: 메타타입: 타입의 타입으로 `Dog.Type`처럼 쓰며, 그 값인 `Dog.self`로 타입을 다른 값처럼 넘길 수 있음

Mirror - A Swift type that lets code look at the stored properties of any value, with their names and values, while the app runs.
한국어: Mirror: 앱이 실행되는 동안 어떤 값이든 저장 프로퍼티의 이름과 값을 들여다볼 수 있게 해 주는 Swift 타입

In this video, Mina and Jake read a debug logger, find out what a type looks like as a value and decide where a Mirror does not belong, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.
Mina와 Jake의 채팅 스타일 대화와 화면 속 Swift 코드로 배워요.

landscape.hook: Declared as Any, printed as Order. Can you explain it in English?

dialogue.title: What does log print?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, what does `log` print for an `Order`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: First the Runtime Type. `x` is declared as `Any`, but it prints `Order`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So that call gives back a string?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No, it gives a Metatype, the type itself as a value.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's a Mirror. It reads the stored properties while the app runs.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, each child has a `label` and a `value`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Could we use a Mirror to save orders to disk?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I wouldn't. It's built for debuggers and playgrounds, not saving data.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Runtime Type for the real type, Metatype as its value, and Mirror for the properties.
Declared as `Any`, but the Runtime Type is still `Order`.
